verdict.rationale: Bitwarden ships a first-party MCP server that gives AI assistants access to password manager functionality, and a hands-on probe completed its stdio initialize handshake. That lets a user drive the vault in natural language through an external AI client. However, Bitwarden's own apps have no built-in natural-language interface; the language understanding comes from a third-party assistant. Missing for 10: a native natural-language command interface in Bitwarden's own clients, documentation of which vault operations work via natural language, and independent hands-on evidence of real natural-language tasks succeeding beyond the handshake.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can operate the product with natural-language commands

citations.quote: A Model Context Protocol (MCP) server that provides AI assistants with secure access to Bitwarden password manager functionality through two complementary interfaces:
